overview: This bill, called the Put America on Commission Act, would create an Office of Whistleblower Awards inside the Small Business Administration (SBA) to reward people who report fraud in COVID-era SBA loan programs, such as Paycheck Protection Program loans and disaster loans. If a tip that the office passes to the SBA's inspector general (its internal watchdog) leads to a final conviction, settlement or plea deal, the whistleblower would get 10 percent of the money recovered, or 15 percent if the wrongdoer is foreign. People convicted or settling such cases would also owe an extra penalty equal to 30 percent of the loan amounts involved. The bill protects whistleblowers from retaliation, bars awards to people who planned the fraud themselves, and ends the program once the last COVID loan cases are finished. As of February 20, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say paying for tips is a proven way to uncover fraud, and this would help recover taxpayer money lost to pandemic loan schemes at no added cost, since awards come from money collected from wrongdoers.
against: Critics say a large added penalty and cash rewards could encourage weak or self-interested tips, and the new office adds bureaucracy for a program that is winding down.
